pl-l2d41c1-d1e108.summary: Asks, since intention makes the good work and faith directs intention, whether every intention and work of those without faith is evil; where there is no faith there seems to be no good intention or work.

pl-l2d41c1-d1e111.summary: Reports some who reasonably hold that all human actions and wills without faith are evil, and become good with faith.
claims: Without faith all acts are evil.

pl-l2d41c1-d1e114.summary: Cites 'whatever is not from faith is sin' and Augustine's exposition: the whole life of unbelievers is sin, and nothing is good without the highest good; where knowledge of eternal truth is lacking, virtue is false even in the best morals.

pl-l2d41c1-d1e118.summary: Cites James: whoever offends in one, charity, is guilty of all; so for one lacking faith and charity every action is sin, not referred to charity, and so not done as it ought; he keeps no command, since none is kept without charity.
claims: Without charity no command is kept.

pl-l2d41c1-d1e121.summary: Cites Augustine on Galatians: keeping the law, not killing, not committing adultery, and good morals, cannot be fulfilled without charity and hope; so one without charity and faith fulfills no command and does no good work, since without faith it is impossible to please God, and every good pleases God.

pl-l2d41c1-d1e128.summary: Objects with Augustine: in servile fear good is done but not well, so one without charity does good; and on the turtledove finding a nest, he says Jews, heretics, and pagans do good works, clothing the naked and feeding the poor, but not in the nest of the Church, faith, so their young are trampled.
claims: Augustine says unbelievers do good works.

pl-l2d41c1-d1e131.summary: Reports their answer: such works without charity are called good not because they are good when so done, but because they would be good if done otherwise; they are good in kind but evil by affection.
claims: Such works are good in kind, evil by affection.

pl-l2d41c1-d1e134.summary: Reports others, who divide acts three ways, holding that works done to support nature are always good; Augustine's calling them evil with evil causes means those doing them sin, not that the works are evil; and 'intention makes the good work' means good as rewardable for life, not the only good work.
claims: Works supporting nature are always good.
Good can mean rewardable for life.

pl-l2d41c1.summary: Asks whether every intention and work of those without faith is evil, since intention makes the good work and faith directs intention. Some reasonably hold that all actions and wills of a person without faith are evil: 'whatever is not from faith is sin' (Rom 14:23), and Augustine says the whole life of unbelievers is sin and virtue without knowledge of eternal truth is false; he who offends in one, charity, is guilty of all, since what is not referred to charity is not done as it ought; without faith it is impossible to please God. Against this, Augustine says the servile do good but not well, and that Jews, heretics, and pagans do good works like clothing the naked, but outside the nest of the Church. The first group answers that such works are called good because they would be good if done otherwise, being good in kind but evil by affection. Those with the threefold division hold that works done in support of nature are always good, and that 'intention makes the good work' means good as rewardable for life.
claims: Intention makes the good work, and faith directs intention.
Some hold all acts and wills of those without faith are evil.
Whatever is not from faith is sin.
Without charity no command is kept.
Augustine also says unbelievers do good works outside the Church.
Works without charity are good in kind but evil by affection, on one view.
On another view, works supporting nature are always good, and 'good work' can mean rewardable for life.
